Photo from Getty-181828180 Contents Contents 1 Vehicles 2 Aviation, Marine and Rail 3 Public Transit 4 Fuels 5 Considerations and Resources 6 7 National Laboratory of the Rockies | 2 Vehicles Vehicles Electric Vehicles Electric Vehicles • Electric vehicles (EVs) use electricity, which improves fuel economy and lowers fuel costs. (DOE, n.d.) • There are 4 types of EVs: ◦ Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) ◦ Plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) ◦ Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) ◦ Fuel Cell Electrics Vehicles (FCEVs) National Laboratory of the Rockies | 4 Types of EVs Types of EVs BEV • Powered by an electric motor that uses energy stored in a battery. • The battery is charged by plugging the vehicle in to charging equipment. • Can travel about 100 to 400 miles on a single charge, depending on model and battery options. PHEV • Powered by an internal combustion engine and an electric motor that uses energy stored in a battery. • Battery is charged by plugging the vehicle into charging equipment. HEV • Powered by an internal combustion engine and an electric motor that uses energy stored in a battery. • The battery is charged through regenerative braking, not by plugging in. FCEV • Powered by a propulsion system similar to that of electric vehicles, where energy stored as hydrogen is converted to electricity by the fuel cell. • Fueled with pure hydrogen gas stored in a tank on the vehicle.
